description: Ground truth for evaluating a security review of this fixture. 'findings' must be reported; 'traps' are safe or out-of-context patterns that must NOT be reported as vulnerabilities.

findings.title: next 15.2.2 is affected by React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182 / CVE-2025-66478, unauthenticated RCE in the App Router) and many later advisories; upgrade to 15.5.27 or 16.3.8
Admin area protected only by middleware; next 15.2.2 is affected by the CVE-2025-29927 middleware bypass, exposing all accounts and the unauthenticated deleteAccount action
updateMemberRole Server Action lets any logged-in user change any profile's role (no owner check, no team scoping, role not allow-listed)
Invoice IDOR across teams: the invoice page reads any invoice by id and deleteInvoice deletes any invoice id (owner of any team); the id arrives via an unencrypted .bind argument
Mass assignment in updateProfile: Object.fromEntries(formData) written to the profile lets users set role, teamId or apiToken
updateProfile returns the full profile row (apiToken, mfaRecoveryCodes, stripeCustomerId) to the client
Public profile page passes the entire Profile row to the ProfileCard Client Component, leaking email, apiToken and MFA recovery codes in the RSC payload
Supabase service-role key in a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable, used by a client component (AvatarUploader), so it is inlined into the browser bundle and bypasses RLS
next.config env inlines BILLING_API_TOKEN, and BillingWidget (a client component) sends it from the browser
Files route authorizes with supabase.auth.getSession() (unverified cookie) and then uses the service-role client, so a forged session cookie lists and signs any user's documents
unstable_cache revenue report captures teamId from the closure but keys on 'revenue-report' only, serving one team's revenue and customers to every team
Unauthenticated GET /api/revalidate lets anyone revalidate any path or tag
Stored XSS: post bodies rendered with marked (no sanitization) via dangerouslySetInnerHTML
XSS via JSON.stringify of displayName/teamName inside an inline script in the dashboard layout (</script> breakout)
Full-read SSRF in /api/preview: any logged-in user can fetch arbitrary URLs (internal hosts, cloud metadata) and receive the response
Image optimizer allows any http/https host with dangerouslyAllowSVG and contentDispositionType 'inline' and no contentSecurityPolicy: SVG XSS on the app origin plus optimizer abuse/SSRF
Open redirect in the auth callback: NextResponse.redirect(new URL(next, request.url)) with the next query parameter
CSRF on the cookie-authenticated email-change Route Handler: accepts form posts with no Origin check while the Supabase auth cookies are SameSite=None
/api/export reflects any Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, so any site can read the team's invoice export (cookies are SameSite=None)
Draft mode can be enabled by anyone (no secret on /api/draft), exposing unpublished posts
Unauthenticated Pages Router API /api/v1/members returns any team's members with emails (middleware matcher excludes /api, handler has no auth)

optional.title: productionBrowserSourceMaps: true publishes client source maps
No CSP or other security headers configured; X-Powered-By not disabled
No rate limiting on the link preview endpoint or other expensive operations
15.x is Maintenance LTS (fixes only on 15.5.x); plan migration to 16.x and proxy.ts
lib/supabase/admin.ts and other privileged modules lack import 'server-only'

traps.title: Stripe webhook verifies the signature with constructEvent over the raw body; no CSRF protection needed
href={user.website} in ProfileCard: the App Router renders with React 19, which neutralizes javascript: URLs in href
Comments rendered with react-markdown (no rehype-raw, default urlTransform) are safe
Inline archive Server Action uses an encrypted closure and re-checks team ownership (updateMany scoped by teamId)
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY in the browser client are meant to be public
Announcement uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML on DOMPurify-sanitized HTML
searchInvoices uses a Prisma $queryRaw tagged template (parameterized) scoped by teamId
force-cache on the public exchange-rate fetch (no credentials, not personalized)
Server Action forms have no CSRF token; Next.js enforces POST plus the Origin/Host check (allowedOrigins is a single exact host)
.env.example contains only placeholder values (not committed secrets)
signOut Server Action has no auth check; it only ends the caller's own session
Middleware and the DAL verify the user with supabase.auth.getUser(), not getSession()
